Last Friday (the 21st), on the day of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China case verdict, a woman was taken away in a police vehicle during early morning queueing to attend the hearing. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of his duty," and "with seditious intent."

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the queue, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue had "clothing that appeared to have some seditious elements," and immediately escorted her onto a police vehicle. While taking the woman away, multiple police officers repeatedly asked reporters to leave, saying they would "take you to the press area," while extending the orange cordon towards Ying Wa Street. It was only after the woman had boarded the police vehicle that they retracted the cordon. That day, a "court observation volunteer" who had been queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese text printed on it.

The Collective (集誌社) enquired with the police as to why the woman was taken away, and whether she had been arrested. The police responded this morning (the 24th) stating that during a security operation at the West Kowloon Court on August 21, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of his duty," and "with seditious intent," and was detained for investigation.
